x: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Commentary on the sūra "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."
The discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High (1), who created and proportioned (2), and who determined and guided (3), and who brought forth the pasture (4), and made it dark-hued stubble (5). We shall make you recite, so you will not forget (6), except what God wills; He knows the open and what is hidden (7)
The people of interpretation differed over the interpretation of His saying
h
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High

Some of them said: its meaning is "magnify your Lord, the Most High, than whom there is no lord higher and greater." And some of them, when they recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
Mention of those who said this.

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abū Bishr informed us, from Saʿīd b.
m: Jubayr, from Ibn ʿUmar, that he used to recite: (Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High — glory be to my Lord, the Most High — who created and proportioned). He said: And it is so in the reading of Ubayy b. Kaʿb.
Ibn Bashshār related to us, saying:

c: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, saying: Sufyān told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from al-Suddī, from ʿAbd Khayr, who said:
m: I heard ʿAlī, may God be pleased with him, recite
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
, and he said: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying:

c: Ḥakkām told us, from ʿAnbasa, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hamdānī,
m: that Ibn ʿAbbās, when he recited
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." And when he recited
I swear by the Day of Resurrection
Is not that One able to give life to the dead?
[al-Qiyāma: 40], he would say: "Glory to You, O God — yes indeed!"

c: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ, when he recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying:

c: Mihrān told us, from Khārija, from Dāwūd, from Ziyād b.
m: ʿAbd Allāh, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās recite in the sunset prayer: (Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High — glory be to my Lord, the Most High).

x: Rather, its meaning is: "Hold exalted, O Muḥammad, the name of your Lord, the Most High, so that you name nothing else by it."
By this He forbids him to do what the polytheists did in naming their gods — one of them al-Lāt and another al-ʿUzzā.
Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Hold God exalted above what the polytheists say of Him," as He said:
h
And do not revile those who call upon others besides God, lest they revile God in transgression, without knowledge
[al-Anʿām: 108]. They said: the meaning is "glorify your Lord, the Most High," and they said: the name is not the thing named [i.e. ism here is not a distinct referent].

Others said: Hold exalted your naming of your Lord, the Most High, O Muḥammad, and your remembrance of Him, so that you do not mention Him except while humbly submissive to Him. They said: what is meant by "name" is naming (tasmiya), but the noun was put in the place of the verbal noun.
Others said: the meaning of His saying
h
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High

is "pray, O Muḥammad, with the remembrance of your Lord," meaning: pray while you are remembering Him, and in awe and fear of Him. The most correct of these views in our opinion is the view of those who said: its meaning is "hold exalted the name of your Lord, so that you do not call by it gods and idols," on account of the reports I have mentioned from the Messenger of God ﷺ and from the Companions that when they recited this they said "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High." For it is plain from this that its meaning, in their understanding, was
n
"magnify the name of your Lord and hold Him exalted."

evidence.text: And some of them, when they recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."
He said: And it is so in the reading of Ubayy b. Kaʿb. (1) Ibn Bashshār related to us, saying:

Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda: {Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High}: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God ﷺ, when he recited it, would say: "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

The most correct of these views in our opinion is the view of those who said: its meaning is "hold exalted the name of your Lord, so that you do not call by it gods and idols," on account of the reports I have mentioned from the Messenger of God ﷺ and from the Companions that when they recited this they said "Glory be to my Lord, the Most High."

x: His saying:
h
who created and proportioned
. He says: the One who created all things and proportioned (sawwā) their creation and made it balanced. Taswiya means balancing (taʿdīl).
His saying:
h
and who determined and guided
. The Exalted says: the One who determined His creation, then guided.
The people of interpretation differed over the meaning intended by
h
then guided
Some said: He guided man to the path of good and of evil, and the beasts to their pastures.
Mention of those who said this.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, saying: ʿĪsā told us, [and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan told us, saying: Warqāʾ told us,
m: from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying
: He said: He guided man to wretchedness and to felicity, and guided the cattle to their pastures.
Others said: Rather, its meaning is that He guided the males to the place of coming to the females. We have already mentioned the report to this effect earlier.
The correct view on this in our opinion is that God, by His saying

, was speaking generally of His guidance of His creation, and did not single out one sense to the exclusion of another. He guided them to the path of good and evil, and guided the males to the place of coming to the females; so the report stands in its generality until a report arrives that establishes proof (ḥujja) indicating its restriction. The reciters of the regions agreed on reading the dāl of
with shadda, except al-Kisāʾī, who lightened it.
The correct reading is the one with shadda, because of the consensus of the authority (ḥujja) on it.

evidence.text: The reciters of the regions agreed on reading the dāl of {qaddara} with shadda, except al-Kisāʾī, who lightened it.
(3) The correct reading is the one with shadda, because of the consensus of the authority (ḥujja) on it.

x: His saying:
h
and who brought forth the pasture
. He says: the One who brought forth from the earth the pasture of the cattle — the various kinds of plants and types of herbage.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this.

c: Yaʿqūb b. Mukram related to me, saying: al-Ḥafarī told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from Manṣūr, from Abū Razīn:
Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: and who brought forth the pasture
as you have seen it, between yellow, red and white.

x: His saying:
h
and made it dark-hued stubble (ghuthāʾan aḥwā)
. The Exalted says: and He made that pasture ghuthāʾ. This is what has dried of vegetation
n

and withered, so that the wind carries it off. What is meant here is that He made it dry, crumbled chaff, turning toward ḥuwwa — which is blackness after whiteness or greenness, from the intensity of dryness.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this.

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: : He says: crumbled chaff, changed in colour.
Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying:

c: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, saying: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan told us, saying: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying
. He said: the debris of a flood;

c: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: . He said: it turns to dryness after greenness.

c: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying
: It was herbage and vegetation, green; then it dried and withered, and became dark-hued stubble, which the winds and the floods carry off.

One of the scholars of the speech of the Arabs held that this is a case of postponement whose sense is advancement; that the meaning of the sentence is: "the One who brought forth the pasture dark-green (aḥwā), meaning green verging on black, and then made it stubble after that." He argues for his statement with the verse of Dhū al-Rumma:
A dusky-green meadow (ḥawwāʾ), white-flowered at its centre, watered by the Sharaṭān rains, where the showers dripped and the buds encircled it.
This view — although it is not excluded that what is intensely green among plants may be called "black" by the Arabs — is incorrect in my opinion, because it contradicts

the interpretation of the people of interpretation, and because a word is only given a contrived sense through transposition (advancing and postponing) when it has no intelligible meaning except by advancing it from its place or postponing it. But where it has a sound meaning in its place, there is no reason to seek a contrived sense for it by transposition.

x: His saying:
h
We shall make you recite, so you will not forget (6), except what God wills
. The Exalted says: We shall make you recite, O Muḥammad, this Qurʾān, so that you will not forget it, except what God wills. Then the people of interpretation differed over the meaning of
h
so you will not forget (6), except what God wills

Some said: this is a report from God to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that He will teach him this Qurʾān and keep it for him, and a prohibition from Him against hastening over its recitation, as He — majestic is His praise — said:
h
Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it (16). Upon Us is its collection and its recitation
[al-Qiyāma: 16–17].
Mention of those who said this.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, saying: ʿĪsā told us, and al-Ḥārith related to me, saying: al-Ḥasan told us, saying: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, on His saying
We shall make you recite, so you will not forget
. He said: He used to rehearse the Qurʾān to himself for fear of forgetting.

The proponents of this view said: the sense of the exception in this place bears on forgetting, and the meaning of the sentence is: "so you will not forget, except what God wills that you forget and not recall." They said: and that is what God abrogated of the Qurʾān, lifting its ruling and its recitation.

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: We shall make you recite, so you will not forget
: The Messenger of God ﷺ did not forget anything, except what God willed.

Others said: the meaning of "forgetting" in this place is "leaving." They said: the meaning of the sentence is: "We shall make you recite, O Muḥammad, so you will not leave acting upon any of it, except what God wills that you leave acting upon, of what We abrogate." One of the scholars of Arabic said of this:
God did not will that he forget
anything. It is like His saying:
abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills

[Hūd: 108], and He does not will [it]. He said: and in ordinary speech you say, "I will give you everything you ask, except what I wish," or "unless I wish to withhold it from you" — the intention being that you will not withhold it, and will not will anything of the sort. He said: and on this footing run oaths: exception is made in them, while the oath-taker's intention is completion.

The view that is more correct in my opinion is that of those who said: its meaning is "so you will not forget, except that We will to make you forget it by abrogating and lifting it." I say that this is more correct because it is the most apparent of its meanings.

x: His saying:
h
He knows the open and what is hidden
. The Exalted says: God knows the open part of your deeds, O Muḥammad — what you have manifested and made public —
h
and what is hidden
. He says: and what you conceal
n

of it, so that you did not manifest it, of what you kept secret. He says: He knows all your deeds, their secret and their public. He says: so beware lest He find you engaged, in any of your states, in other than what He has permitted you.
The discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And We shall ease you toward the easy way (8). So remind, if the reminder benefits (9), he who fears will be reminded (10), and the most wretched will avoid it (11), who will enter the greatest Fire (12), then will neither die in it nor live (13)
The Exalted says: and We shall make easy for you, O Muḥammad, the doing of good, and that is al-yusrā. Al-yusrā is the feminine form (fuʿlā) of yusr ("ease").
His saying:
h
So remind, if the reminder benefits
. The Exalted says: so remind God's servants, O Muḥammad, of His greatness, and admonish them and warn them of His punishment,
h
if the reminder benefits
. He says: if the reminder benefits those whom I have made you despair of their faith — the reminder will not benefit them.
His saying:
h
So remind
. It is a command from God to His Prophet ﷺ to remind all people. Then He said: "if the reminder benefits" those whom I have made you despair of their faith.
His saying:
h
He who fears will be reminded
. He — majestic is His praise — says: he will be reminded, O Muḥammad, when you remind those whom I commanded you to remind, who fears God and dreads His punishment,
h
and will avoid it
. He says: and will avoid the reminder
h
the most wretched
; meaning the more wretched of the two groups:
h
who will enter the greatest Fire
. And they are those whom the reminder did not benefit.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this.

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: So remind, if the reminder benefits (9), he who fears will be reminded
: So fear God! No servant ever feared God but that He reminded him.
And the most wretched will avoid it
this reminder out of disdain for it and hatred of its people, except one manifestly wretched.

x: His saying:
h
who will enter the greatest Fire
. He says: the one who comes to the Fire of Hell, and that is the greatest Fire. By "greatest" He means [in the intensity of]
n
heat and pain.
His saying:
h
then will neither die in it nor live

. He says: then he will neither die in the greatest Fire nor live. That is because the soul of each of them will come to be in his throat: it will not come out, so that it parts from him and he dies, nor return to its place in the body, so that he lives. It was also said: he will not die in it and so find rest, nor live a life that benefits him.

Others said: this was said because the Arabs, when they described a man as having fallen into a severe hardship, would say, "He is neither alive nor dead." So God addressed them with what had come to run in that manner of their speech.
The discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

He who purifies himself has succeeded (14), and remembers the name of his Lord and prays (15). But you prefer the life of this world (16), while the Hereafter is better and more lasting (17). This is indeed in the earlier scrolls (18), the scrolls of Abraham and Moses (19)

He — majestic is His praise — says: he has attained success and reached his goal who has purified himself of unbelief and of disobedience to God, and has acted as God commanded him and fulfilled His obligations.
A group of the people of interpretation said something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this.

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
. He says: whoever has purified himself of polytheism.
Muḥammad b. al-Muthannā related to us, saying:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī told us, saying: Hishām told us, from al-Ḥasan,
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
. He said: whoever's deeds were pure.
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying:

c: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd al-Ḥakam related to me, saying:

c: Ḥafṣ b. ʿUmar al-ʿAdanī told us, from al-Ḥakam, from ʿIkrima,
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
: whoever says "there is no god but God."
Others said: Rather, its meaning is: he has succeeded who has paid the zakāh of his wealth.

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from ʿAlī b.
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
. He said: Whoever is able to give a small gift (yarkhaḍa)
let him do so; then let him stand and pray.
Muḥammad b. ʿUmāra al-Rāzī related to us, saying:

c: Abū Nuʿaym told us, saying: Sufyān told us, from ʿAlī b.
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
. He said: whoever gave a small gift.
Muḥammad b. ʿUmāra related to us, saying:

c: ʿUthmān b. Saʿīd b. Murra told us, saying: Zuhayr told us, from Abū Isḥāq, from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, who said:
m: When a beggar comes to one of you while he intends to pray, let him put his zakāh before his prayer, for God says:
He who purifies himself has succeeded (14), and remembers the name of his Lord and prays
. So whoever is able to put some zakāh before his prayer, let him do so.

c: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: He who purifies himself has succeeded
: a man purified himself through his wealth, and pleased his Creator.
Others said: Rather, what is meant by this is the zakāh of the fast-breaking (zakāt al-fiṭr).

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: ʿAmr b. ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd al-Āmulī related to me, saying: Marwān b. Muʿāwiya told us, from Abū Khaldah, who said:
m: I went in to see Abū al-ʿĀliya, and he said to me: "When you set out tomorrow morning for the festival (ʿīd), pass by me." So I passed by him, and he said: "Have you eaten anything?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Have you poured water over yourself?" I said: "Yes." He said: "Then tell me what you did with your zakāh." I said: "I have already sent it off." He said: "It was only for this that I wanted you." Then he recited:
He who purifies himself has succeeded (14), and remembers the name of his Lord and prays
, and said: "The people of Medina see no charity better than it, nor than the giving of water to drink."

x: His saying:
h
and remembers the name of his Lord and prays
The people of interpretation differed over the interpretation of His saying
h
and remembers the name of his Lord and prays
Some said: its meaning is that he affirmed God's oneness.
Mention of those who said this.

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: and remembers the name of his Lord and prays
. He says: he affirmed the oneness of God, glory be to Him.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is that he remembered God, called upon Him, and turned to Him in longing. The correct view on this is to say: he remembered God and so affirmed His oneness, and called upon Him and turned to Him in longing; for all of that is part of remembrance of God, and God the Exalted did not single out one kind of His remembrance to the exclusion of another.

x: His saying:
h
and prays
The people of interpretation differed over the interpretation of this.
Some said: what is meant is that he prayed the five prayers.
Mention of those who said this.

c: ʿAlī related to me, saying: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, saying: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: . He says: he prayed the five prayers.

x: Others said: what is meant is the festival prayer on the day of the fast-breaking.

Others said: Rather, what is meant is: "and remembers the name of his Lord and so supplicates." They said: "prayer" (ṣalāt) here means supplication (duʿāʾ). The correct view is to say: what is meant by His saying
h
and prays
is the prayers, and the remembrance of God within them by praise, glorification and supplication.
His saying:
h
But you prefer the life of this world
. He says to the people: Rather you prefer, O people, the adornment of the life of this world over the Hereafter,
h
while the Hereafter is better
for you
h
and more lasting

. He says: and the adornment of the Hereafter is better for you, O people, and longer-lasting in duration; for the life of this world is perishing, while the Hereafter is enduring, neither exhausted nor ending.
The people of interpretation said something like what we have said.
Mention of those who said this.

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: But you prefer the life of this world
: so people chose the immediate, except those whom God protected.

x: His saying:
h
while the Hereafter is better
: in goodness;
h
and more lasting
: in endurance.
n
Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying:

c: Yaḥyā b. Wāḍiḥ told us, saying: Abū Ḥamza told us, from ʿAṭāʾ, from ʿArfaja al-Thaqafī, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Masʿūd to recite to me; it was
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
But you prefer the life of this world

, he stopped reciting and turned to his companions and said: "We preferred this world over the Hereafter." The people fell silent. He said: "We preferred this world because we saw its adornment, its women, its food and its drink, while the Hereafter was withdrawn from us; so we chose this immediate thing and left the deferred."
The reciters differed over the reading of His saying
But you prefer the life of this world
. Most of the reciters of the regions read
with the tāʾ, except Abū ʿAmr, who read it with the yāʾ
and said: he means the most wretched ones.

The reading that I do not prefer anything over is the tāʾ, because of the consensus of the authority among the reciters on it. And it is reported that in the reading of Ubayy it is: (Rather, you — you prefer).
That too is a witness to the soundness of the reading with the tāʾ.

evidence.text: (3) The reciters differed over the reading of His saying {But you prefer the life of this world}.
Most of the reciters of the regions read {tuʾthirūna} with the tāʾ, except Abū ʿAmr, who read it with the yāʾ (1) and said: he means the most wretched ones.
(2) The reading that I do not prefer anything over is the tāʾ, because of the consensus of the authority among the reciters on it.
And it is reported that in the reading of Ubayy it is: (Rather, you — you prefer).
(3) That too is a witness to the soundness of the reading with the tāʾ.

x: His saying:
h
This is indeed in the earlier scrolls
The people of interpretation differed over what is pointed to by His saying
h
this
Some said: it points to the verses that are in
h
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
Mention of those who said this.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from his father, from ʿIkrima:
m: This is indeed in the earlier scrolls (18), the scrolls of Abraham and Moses
. He says: the verses that are in
Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High
Others said: the account (qiṣṣa) of this sūra.

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Mihrān told us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya:
m: This is indeed in the earlier scrolls (18), the scrolls of Abraham and Moses
. He said: the account of this sūra is in the earlier scrolls.
Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "this which God decreed
in this sūra is in the earlier scrolls."

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda,
m: This is indeed in the earlier scrolls
. He said: This which God decreed
in this sūra is in the earlier scrolls,
the scrolls of Abraham and Moses
Others said: Rather, what is meant is that His saying
while the Hereafter is better and more lasting

x: Mention of those who said this.

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda,
m: This is indeed in the earlier scrolls
. He said: The books of God have followed one another, as you hear, [saying] that the Hereafter is better and more lasting.

c: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying:
m: Ibn Zayd said, on His saying
This is indeed in the earlier scrolls (18), the scrolls of Abraham and Moses
. He said: in the scrolls that God sent down upon Abraham and Moses, [it is stated] that the Hereafter is better than the first.
The most correct of the views on this is the view of those who said: His saying
He who purifies himself has succeeded (14), and remembers the name of his Lord and prays (15). But you prefer the life of this world (16), while the Hereafter is better and more lasting

is in the earlier scrolls: the scrolls of Abraham, the Intimate Friend of the Most Merciful, and the scrolls of Moses, son of ʿImrān. I say that this is more correct than the others because "this" (hādhā) is a pointer to what is present, so its being a pointer to what is nearest to it is more fitting than its being a pointer to something else. As for al-ṣuḥuf, it is the plural of ṣaḥīfa, and what is meant by it is the books of Abraham and Moses.

c: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazīd told us, saying: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, from Abū al-Jald, who said:
m: The scrolls of Abraham were sent down on the first night of Ramaḍān; the Torah was sent down when six nights of Ramaḍān had passed; the Psalms (al-Zabūr) were sent down
on the twelfth night; the Gospel (al-Injīl) on the eighteenth; and the Criterion (al-Furqān, the Qurʾān) on the twenty-fourth.
End of the commentary on the sūra "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High."

notes.en: A rawdah qarhaʾ is a garden with white flowers in its middle; qarhaʾ is also said of a place where vegetation has appeared. Ashratiyya means that it was rained upon by al-Sharatan, the two stars of Aries that form its horns; beside the northern one is a small star. Wakafat means “it dripped.” Al-dhihab is the plural of dhihbah, a rainfall, also said to mean a light shower. See Lisan al-ʿArab, roots q-r-h, sh-r-t, w-k-f, and dh-h-b.
notes.ar: روضة قرحاء: في وسطها نَوْرٌ أبيض. وقيل: القرحاء: التي بدا نبتُها. أشراطية: مُطِرَتْ بالشَّرَطَين، وهما نجمان من الحَمَل وهما قرناه، وإلى جانب الشماليِّ منهما كوكب صغير. وكَفَتْ: قَطَرَتْ. والذِّهاب: جمع ذِهْبَةٍ وهى المَطَرَةُ، وقيل: المطرةُ الضعيفة. اللسان (ق ر ح)، (ش ر ط)، (و ك ف)، (ذ هـ ب).
